title: Accessible Widget Building
description: Create a custom toggle button with proper semantics and keyboard support.
problemStatement:
You need a button that toggles the visibility of a paragraph. Write the HTML for this widget using the most semantic approach.

**Requirements:**
- A button that says "Show details" (or "Hide details" depending on state – initially hidden).
- A paragraph with `id="details"` initially hidden (you can use `hidden` attribute).
- When the button is clicked, JavaScript will toggle the paragraph (you don't need to write JS; just set up the HTML so it's ready).
- The button must have an `aria-expanded` attribute that reflects the current state (start with `aria-expanded="false"`).
- The button must have an `aria-controls` attribute pointing to the paragraph's `id`.
- Include a descriptive `aria-label` on the button (e.g., "Show more details").
- Ensure the button is keyboard accessible (it's a `<button>`, which is natively focusable).

Write the HTML for this widget (just the button and paragraph).
hints: Use `<button>` element – it's focusable and has click/Enter/Space events built‑in.
`aria-controls="details"` links the button to the controlled element.
The `hidden` attribute on the paragraph hides it until JS removes it.
expectedOutput: An accessible toggle button with appropriate ARIA attributes.
solutionCode: This is the detailed information that can be toggled.
